claims.statement: The IDE is a static page with no build step because wasm/pkg and rtl/pkg are committed, and it must be served over HTTP because the compiled modules are fetched; a file:// open stays on the JavaScript core.

index.html loads the assembler, disassembler, optimizer, JS core, the flash-assets/gfx-loader/tile-engine/D16D-image scripts and the panel scripts in order, then an inline module imports and initialises the WASM and RTL packages.
deep16_ui_core.js ends with a DOMContentLoaded handler that constructs DeepWebUI, resets and runs it, and the editor textarea ships with a small sample program so the page is live on load.

DeepWebUI owns one assembler, disassembler and JS simulator, the memory/register/screen panel objects, a lazily created FiT tile engine, cached D16D sources, the tile clock and the console mode, autoloads the boot ROM and caps the transcript at 50 entries.

The stored core selector is coreName (js, wasm or rtl), with useWasm kept only as a derived flag, and the selection is persisted under deep16_core with the legacy deep16_use_wasm boolean read when the new key is absent.

Switching cores mirrors state rather than resetting: syncStateIntoCore calls init, load_program, set_segments, set_psw and set_registers in that order, with PSW before registers because set_registers resolves element 15 through PSW.S.
run() calls ensureTerminalCore first and, in terminal mode, assembles the editor text when it differs from the last assembled source so Run cannot execute a stale image.

Both run loops use a 10 ms setInterval and instructionsPerTick(): 200 steps in screen/terminal mode and 6,000 in Tiles mode; a separate 60 Hz tile clock sets the display status and ticks the engine, and neither loop uses requestAnimationFrame or a worker.
Both loops compute the physical CS:PC before each instruction and stop when it matches a breakpoint, resuming by stepping over the breakpoint once.

The compiled-core loop reads back each observed store with get_recent_access and get_memory_word, writes it into simulator.memory, routes screen-memory writes to the screen panel, and tracks a dirty address range.
step() executes one instruction on the active core, resolves the shadow PC when PSW.S is set, recentres the 64-word memory window, and forces running on so a step works after a halt.
reset() clears the run interval, cancels an in-flight file upload, resets both the active core and the JS simulator, restores the shipped image, re-reads the echo flag and recentres on the reset PC.
The memory panel starts with a breakpoint at 0x00100, toggles breakpoints on click, draws a B in its own column and lists them in the header.
Each memory row is shown through the disassembler and conditional jumps print their resolved target, while the panel highlights the last data access and the PC.
The register panel prints R0-R15 with the aliases FP/R12, SP/R13, LR/R14 and PC/R15, and maps PSW bits DE=15, DS=10, S=5, I=4, C=3, V=2, Z=1, N=0 to the checkbox row.

The screen panel draws the 80x24 buffer at 0xF1000, 1920 words ending at 0xF177F, with 4-bit foreground/background in the high byte, attribute 0 meaning default, and reverse video (CURSOR_ATTR 0x7000) standing in for a cursor.
The screen panel keeps a per-cell drawn cache so a refresh touches only cells that changed, avoiding a 1920-span repaint every tick.

SerialTerminal renders the UART byte stream into an 80x24 grid, supporting printable ASCII with autowrap, CR, LF with scroll, BS, TAB, CSI J clear-and-home and CSI H/f home-only while dropping every other escape.

The Trace button is one gate for panel updates: with trace off, updateAllDisplays drains the UART and returns, so the machine and terminal keep running while registers, memory and screen stop redrawing.

One persisted console mode (deep16_console) selects screen, terminal or tiles; it changes the assembler defines, what the Screen tab shows and where input goes, and toggling it rebuilds the editor source.
File loading and saving use the File System Access API with a hidden file input and download-link fallback, keeping the file handle so Save writes in place and Save As replaces it.
A .fth or .forth file is not opened in the editor but queued as keystrokes for the running kernel, with the check in code because iOS Safari does not enforce the dialog accept list.

Examples come from asm/examples.json, are grouped by category, and are fetched from asm/<filename> with cache no-store; loading one fills the editor and switches to the Editor tab, and the D16D entry also fetches the showcase, Flappy and Pac-Man sources.
The Docs menu fetches doc/Deep16-Arch.md, FORTH.md or doc/User-man.md and renders it in an overlay with a built-in Markdown renderer, closing on Escape or an outside click.
The editor is a textarea with a highlight overlay and a tab width persisted as deep16.tabSize.

js/deep16_worker.js implements a complete message protocol for INIT, LOAD_PROGRAM, RUN, STEP, RESET and STOP, but no new Worker is constructed anywhere, workerRun posts to an undefined this.worker, and no script tag loads the file.
Settings persist under deep16_core, deep16_use_wasm, deep16_console and deep16.tabSize, with every storage access wrapped so disabled storage degrades to defaults.

A hidden focusable #terminal-kbd-hook input exists because iOS only raises the soft keyboard for a real input focused inside a tap; tapping the screen focuses it and key events reach handleTerminalKey.

Tiles mode attaches a Deep16TileEngine to the simulator, loads the generated graphics blob, and builds the D16D image from the kernel plus the four fetched showcase sources; the browser builder's bakePacman flag defaults to false and is used by the headless renderer to bake a preview at 0x4330.
